{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABYb5_ng", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhB_7IU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 17, "title": "Add a reproducible LoRA positive-control experiment for SQL code generation", "body": "## Problem

The existing Apple Silicon LoRA workflow successfully reproduced an improvement for **freight-text → JSON extraction** (107/150 → 150/150). However, our earlier general Python/MBPP/HumanEval fine-tuning did not improve coding accuracy. The next step should be a **real code-generation task with published positive before/after evidence**, not another open-ended hyperparameter search.

A concrete reference is [W-Kaski/qwen-qlora-sql-benchmark](https://github.com/W-Kaski/qwen-qlora-sql-benchmark), which reports 500-example **normalized SQL exact-match** results using `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` on `b-mc2/sql-create-context`: base **4.4%**, rank-8 LoRA **68.4%** (also 98.0% → 99.2% SQL parse validity). These are third-party single-seed results, **not** yet our results and **not** SQL execution accuracy. The reference uses NVIDIA/4-bit NF4; our target is Apple Silicon/MLX. The quantization/training framework difference may prevent exact numerical reproduction.

## Expected outcome

Implement a separate, copy-and-run **natural language + table schema → SQL query** LoRA experiment in `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, using Apple Silicon / MLX, a small model, and an immutable, auditable dataset/configuration. Provide clean base-model vs fresh-LoRA measurements showing whether this locally reproduced task improves **generated SQL accuracy**, distinguishing syntax, exact-string agreement and actual execution semantics.

This is an **intermediate, specialized code-generation positive control**. It is not evidence of general Python/3D-programming ability and it must not replace the already working freight example.

## Context

- Target repository: `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, default branch `main`. Its README currently focuses on a successful Qwen2.5-0.5B shipment JSON extraction demo, with prior Python code-generation code retained as legacy. [PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/pull/12) may still be open; inspect current state at implementation time. Do not delete or break either existing experiment or collaboration guidance.
- Published reference: https://github.com/W-Kaski/qwen-qlora-sql-benchmark, reference HEAD observed as `b90759ab610ae29a0e8744098eda6ea0d559df36`. Verify its actual configurations, evaluation and license before implementation; use an immutable upstream revision and record differences.
- Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/b-mc2/sql-create-context (CC-BY-4.0, fields `context`, `question`, `answer`; 78,577 rows reported). Pin source revision/checksums and required attribution.
- Original reference: 5,000 training and 500 held-out records, one epoch, rank-8 LoRA (original CUDA NF4), completion-only supervision, source prompt/evaluation protocol. Source also reports a small 30-case manually curated SQLite execution sanity check for another adapter, **not a 500-case execution benchmark**.
- Base model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` (Apache-2.0), use the same pinned model/revision for base and adapted inference. Avoid comparing an unquantized base against a 4-bit adapter without accounting for quantization differences.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md); write all new Issue/PR, commit messages and repository documentation in English.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Reference and data
- [ ] Review and record the exact source recipe, model/quantization, chat template, prompt, training config, split selection, evaluator, normalization, and dataset/license provenance. Pin immutable source/model/dataset revisions where possible. Explicitly identify divergences between CUDA NF4 and MLX quantization/training; **do not claim bit-identical reproduction**.
- [ ] Deterministically create or verify a **5,000 training / 500 held-out** SQL task split (plus validation only if used by the chosen trainer). Document filtering, selection seed, unique IDs, hashes and split integrity; prevent duplicate/near-duplicate schema-question examples leaking into evaluation. Do not alter the held-out cohort after inspecting predictions.
- [ ] Format training examples with schema + question as input and **reference SQL only as target**, with correct completion-only loss masking. No reference SQL or evaluation answers in generation prompts.

### Reproducible Apple Silicon training and evaluation
- [ ] Provide commands to install/check the native Apple Silicon MLX environment, download the pinned model (4-bit when feasible), prepare the dataset, run a **fresh rank-8 LoRA training session** roughly matching the reference's one-epoch recipe, then evaluate baseline and adapter and generate a before/after report.
- [ ] Keep base and adapted inference strictly paired: same model weights/quantization, prompt/chat template, held-out examples, deterministic decoding, token budget, parser/normalization and library versions. Store settings and checksums in experiment receipts. Model weights and adapter files remain ignored local artifacts.
- [ ] Calculate per-example and aggregate **normalized SQL exact match**, **SQL parse validity**, changed-item counts (fail→pass/pass→fail) and failure categories, including denominator/numerator and signed percentage-point deltas. Explain that exact match can reject semantically equivalent queries.
- [ ] Include a **small, controlled SQLite execution-correctness check** for a fixed, disjoint, executable subset or curated fixture with schemas and populated test databases. Score base and adapted queries using the **same seeded data and gold-query results**, isolate execution safely, and reject non-read-only SQL. Record the cohort, limitations and any coverage exclusions honestly. Do not present parse validity as proof of semantic correctness or describe this limited sanity check as a full benchmark.
- [ ] Compare our independently measured results with the **upstream-reported 4.4% → 68.4% exact-match** result, with explicit differences and root-cause notes if reproduction fails. **Matching the score or improving is not required for an honest completion**; never manipulate the scorer or test set merely to match published numbers.
- [ ] Maintain separate ignored outputs for training/evaluation, reject accidental overwrites, and preserve the existing freight positive control, historical models/results and open-PR dependencies.

### Scope, tests and documentation
- [ ] Add focused automated tests for deterministic split/leakage checks, prompt and completion masking, SQL parsing/normalization, non-SELECT rejection and execution result scoring, paired metric arithmetic, and result/provenance compatibility.
- [ ] Supply concise README/docs copy-and-run steps and a short explanation of why SQL generation is a narrow but practical code-generation precursor to later Python code-quality work. Keep the main README's successful freight workflow accessible; avoid unrelated refactors, broad tuning sweeps, web apps or service infrastructure.
- [ ] Run applicable unit, lockfile, native-MLX, syntax/Markdown/whitespace checks before merge. Clearly distinguish completed hardware experiments from code-only validation. Submit an Issue-linked PR to `main` and follow the normal review process.

## Optional validation

- On a suitable Apple Silicon Mac, run the entire pinned 500-example comparison before merge, record true duration/memory footprint and training receipts. If model download or training is unavailable, provide runnable commands and report the full run as **not performed**, not as successfully reproduced.
- If the small execution check shows meaningful improvement, consider a later, separately defined broader SQL execution benchmark or Python program-repair experiment. Do not expand this Issue into general programming benchmarks.

## Required post-merge verification

None automatically required. The merge itself does not initiate model downloads, training or benchmark execution.
